correctness.rationale: Kimura–Umemoto Theorem 5.2 supplies b_±(n)=(E_{2n-1}-1)/2 ± 2E_{n-1}, E_n=(lambda^n-lambda^{-n})/(2sqrt3), lambda=2+sqrt3, and the complete permitted exceptional parameter index ranges. The recurrence E_{n+2}=4E_{n+1}-E_n, E_1=1, proves E_n increasing. The within-pair positive gap is 4E_{n-1}; the cross-pair positive gap is D_{2n}-2(E_n+E_{n-1})=1+6E_n^2-2(E_n+E_{n-1})>0. On negative magnitudes the corresponding cross-pair gap is 1+6E_k^2-2(E_{k+1}+E_k)>0 for k≥2 using E_{k+1}<4E_k. Binet terms give each of the two sign-specific branches size proportional to lambda^{2n}, within-pair ratio→1 and between-pair ratio→lambda²; each sign has 2 values per index, hence count log X/log lambda+O(1), total 2log X/log lambda+O(1). Independently generated 44 positive and 44 negative index pairs from the recurrence verify first pairs and interlacing; infinite assertions rest on the inequalities and Binet asymptotics, not the finite test.
